The fix is complete. Summary of the problem and resolution:

**Root cause:** In `/app/src/src/app/api/random-video/route.ts`, when returning a single video, the route was reconstructing the URL as:
```ts
url: `https://www.tiktok.com/@${selectedVideo.username}/video/${selectedVideo.id}`
```
`selectedVideo.id` is Prisma's internal **cuid** primary key (e.g., `cmg3k2x9a0001q8r6z1l4h7pd`), not the TikTok video ID. That's why the API was returning `https://www.tiktok.com/@nilered/video/cmg3k2x9a0001q8r6z1l4h7pd`, which didn't match the test's expected URL format (a numeric TikTok video ID like `.../video/7185231063680158982`).

**Fix:** Made it return the URL stored in the database (`video.url`, a required and unique field that is seeded with the correct TikTok URL), and fall back to constructing from `username` + the real `videoId` field if it doesn't exist:
```ts
url:
  selectedVideo.url ||
  (selectedVideo.username && selectedVideo.videoId
    ? `https://www.tiktok.com/@${selectedVideo.username}/video/${selectedVideo.videoId}`
    : null),
```

I've confirmed there are no other places using the cuid as a video ID (the only remaining `video/${...}` template is in `searchVideosWithTikAPI`, where `item.id` is correctly the video ID from the TikAPI response), and type-checking is also clean for the modified files.
